summary: This resolution sets procedural rules for House floor consideration of H.R. 4690 (repealing federal building energy efficiency standards), H. Res. 1182 (supporting rural communities), H.R. 1897 (amending the Endangered Species Act), and H.R. 5587 (exempting certain geothermal activities from permits and NEPA), by waiving points of order, deeming substitute amendments adopted, limiting each to one hour of debate, and allowing one motion to recommit.

scores.thoughts: The resolution is purely procedural and sets rules for floor consideration of four measures. None of those measures contain appropriations, authorizations, or any other provisions that would expand or contract government spending.
No tax provisions appear in the resolution or the underlying bills it makes in order.

The measures under consideration address energy efficiency standards, the Endangered Species Act, geothermal permitting, and a non-binding resolution on rural communities. None touch healthcare policy.
No reference to firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues exists in the text.
The resolution and the bills it advances contain nothing related to immigration, border security, or legal status.
No provisions address reproductive health, abortion access, or related regulations.
Nothing in the resolution or the four measures concerns defense spending, military construction, or national security authorizations.

Three of the four bills made in order directly alter environmental regulation: H.R. 4690 repeals federal building energy-efficiency performance standards; H.R. 1897 amends the Endangered Species Act to reduce permitting barriers and prioritize resource use; H.R. 5587 waives NEPA review and federal drilling permits for certain geothermal activities. These changes collectively limit environmental regulatory requirements, producing a strong positive alignment with the +1 pole of the scale.
No welfare, nutrition assistance, or social-services provisions are present.
The resolution and underlying measures do not address schools, federal education funding, or school-choice policy.
No drug-enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled-substance language appears.
The text contains no sentencing, policing, or criminal-justice reform provisions.
No trade agreements, tariffs, or import/export rules are addressed.
The resolution is procedural and the bills it advances do not alter revenue or spending in ways that affect the federal deficit trajectory.
No civil-rights, nondiscrimination, or LGBTQ-specific provisions are included.
Foreign assistance is not mentioned.
The resolution and bills contain no election-administration or voting-access language.
No technology regulation, data-privacy, or platform-liability provisions exist.
Nothing in the text addresses collective bargaining, worker protections, or union rules.
The measures do not engage religious exemptions or civil-rights enforcement.
